body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: GPU pool 'west2a-infer-pool-7' kvcache_eviction_rate=0.92, cuda_oom_count=18 in last 5m. Auto-suppression=off. Page -> oncall-primary.
PagerDuty: Incident P12345 created and routed to @Elena S. (oncall-primary).
Elena S.: acked P12345 :white_check_mark: pulling logs now. Noting noisy kvcache evictions + repeated cuda OOM.
Raj K.: any customers impacted?
Elena S.: looking at metrics — serving errors spiked from 0.3% -> 6.8% for requests hitting west2a. Latency also up ~120ms p95. Initial suspicion: aggressive prefetch/batch job filling GPU mem + kvcache churn.
Matt B.: can we start with pool drain and failover to west2b? recommend: `rictl pool drain west2a-infer-pool-7 --grace 30s` then `rictl route --from west2a-infer-pool-7 --to west2b-infer-pool-2 --model open-13b-quant`
Elena S.: running drain now. output:
```
> rictl pool drain west2a-infer-pool-7 --grace 30s
Draining pool west2a-infer-pool-7: started
Active allocs: 24 -> triggering graceful fallback
Triggering route fallback to compatible pools
```
Elena S.: also bumping pool size up temporarily: `rictl pool scale west2a-infer-pool-7 --gpu 2` — doing this as a short-term buffer.
PagerDuty: P12345 acknowledged by Elena S. at 1777654350. No auto-escalation.
Sasha C.: CS watching customer errors. tagging the top hits: cust-482, cust-790. cust-482 reporting higher hallucination/dropouts via support.
Customer Success Bot: customer cust-482 flagged — support ticket T-90812 created, customer notified: "We're investigating increased errors for inference requests in us-west2".
Raj K.: Elena can you paste the relevant tail of nvidia driver log and the runtime stack?
Elena S.: logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-14T22:45:18Z] cuda: [GPU0] CUBLAS_ALLOC_FAILED, alloc_size=1.2GiB
[2026-03-14T22:45:19Z] runtime: kvcache_evictions=938, prefetch_inflight=42
[2026-03-14T22:45:19Z] infer: session=abc123 token_index=512 oom_error=true
[2026-03-14T22:45:20Z] cuda: [GPU1] CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY during kernel launch
```
Elena S.: also seeing continual small allocations from background prefetcher job. suspect a prefetch loop that doesn't respect kvcache budget.
Matt B.: Good call. Mitigation plan: 1) drain + reroute (in progress), 2) throttle prefetcher via /ops endpoint: `POST /ops/prefetcher/throttle {"pool":"west2a-infer-pool-7","rate":0.3}`, 3) temporarily increase kvcache budget for this pool, 4) monitor.
Elena S.: throttled prefetcher now. API response:
```
{ "status": "ok", "throttled_to": 0.3 }
```
Sasha C.: customer impact: cust-482 error rate down from 18% -> 5% after reroute started. cust-790 still at 9%, likely mid-flight requests failed. CS will follow up.
PagerDuty: auto-escalation timer still ok; P12345 remains with primary.
Raj K.: Any sign of memory leak? eviction patterns suggest churn not monotonic growth. check allocator histograms.
Elena S.: allocator histograms attached (summary): rapid spike correlated with prefetcher start_time=22:40Z, then falls after throttle. No long-term leak observed. Root cause likely prefetch config + aggressive prefetch window for this model.
Matt B.: rolling a config change to reduce prefetch_window from 8->4 for open-13b-quant in west2a. command: `rictl config set model/open-13b-quant/prefetch_window 4 --pool west2a-infer-pool-7`
Elena S.: applied config. verifying.
Elena S.: current status: drain complete, active allocs on west2a=2 (internal), most traffic on west2b. cuda_oom_count now 0 in last 2m, kvcache_eviction_rate down to 0.12. p95 latency trending down.
Sasha C.: noting customer-facing message drafted. We'll keep cust-482 and cust-790 in high touch for next 2 hours.
Matt B.: recommend follow-up postmortem: include prefetch tuning, add throttle-as-runbook, and add a metric alert for sustained prefetch_inflight>30 for >1m.
Elena S.: agreed. I'll convert this thread into an incident doc and assign action owners. tagging @Matt B., @Raj K., @Sasha C. for follow-ups.
Customer Success Bot: notifying customers that mitigations are in place and engineering is investigating root cause.
Elena S.: closing ops loop for now — leaving monitoring for 30m. will update if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
